captions.caption: Title card for SM-3 Block IB launch from Aegis Ashore site.
Title card continues for the missile launch at the Pacific Missile Range Facility.
Transition to a dark screen with the AirSource logo in the corner.
Close-up of intense vertical flames during the rocket's ignition.
A large column of bright yellow and orange fire erupts.
Fire and smoke expand as the launch sequence begins.
A steady stream of high-intensity flames moves rapidly upward.
Bright white light is visible at the center of the fire column.
Continued eruption of powerful flames and white light from the engine.
Dense smoke and fire fill the frame during the initial launch phase.
The base of the missile exhaust creates a wall of brilliant fire.
Intense combustion continues with swirling orange and yellow flames.
The pillar of fire remains constant as the rocket pushes off the pad.
Expanding plumes of fire and smoke are seen in a detailed close-up.
The top of the SM-3 missile starts to rise through the intense flames.
The missile quickly ascends, leaving a massive trail of fire behind it.
The rocket body moves out of the top of the frame into the sky.
A massive plume of residual fire lingers at the launch site after ascent.
Billowing orange and black smoke fills the camera's view.
The fire within the smoke clouds begins to fade slightly as it cools.
Thick, dark smoke continues to swirl in the air after the launch.
Glowing orange light is still visible within the expanding smoke plume.
The smoke plume darkens and spreads across the entire frame.
Turbulent clouds of smoke and fire dominate the scene post-launch.
The camera captures the glowing aftermath of the intense rocket launch.
Dense smoke continues to move and dissipate slowly in the air.
A final view of the glowing smoke before the scene changes.
Wide shot of the missile's bright light ascending into the dark sky.
The missile moves higher, appearing as a bright point of light in the twilight.
The engine's glow is clearly visible as it passes through thin clouds.
Transition to a dark screen with the AirSource logo in the corner.
Wide shot of the dark blue twilight sky with the ascending missile.
The missile continues its ascent, looking like a bright star in the sky.
Bright light from the missile's engine shines through the clouds.
The missile moves steadily upward into the higher atmosphere.
The engine's light appears as a bright, elongated shape against the blue sky.
Close-up view of the glowing missile engine as it travels through space.
The Aegis Ashore facility building is shown at twilight.
Lights illuminate the facility as the missile ascends in the background.
The missile's bright trail is seen in the sky above the facility site.
Missile ascent continues, visible as a bright glow in the distance.
The facility structure remains stationary under the cloudy evening sky.
The bright light of the missile moves behind a layer of clouds.
The glowing trail of the missile is still visible through the evening air.
The facility stands prominently against the darkening sky as the launch ends.
Wide shot of the Aegis Ashore site under a cloudy twilight sky.
Stationary shot of the facility building and its illuminated surroundings.
Clouds drift slowly over the illuminated facility structure at night.
Static view of the facility building at the Pacific Missile Range Facility.
Thermal camera view shows a bright heat signature in the sky.
The thermal image tracks the missile's heat against a blue background.
Intense heat from the engine is shown as a bright orange-red spot.
The heat signature moves across the screen, leaving a faint thermal trail.
Several bright thermal points appear, indicating stage separation.
Thermal view of multiple heat sources from the moving missile in flight.
The heat signatures continue to track across the thermal sensor's field.
Intense thermal spots highlight missile components during its ascent.
The thermal camera follows the glowing heat signatures through the sky.
Multiple bright points of heat are visible against the dark background.
Thermal tracking continues as the objects move further away into space.
